newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-POSITIVE TIGANA LOOKING FOR WIN AT INTER-MILAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POSITIVE TIGANA LOOKING FOR WIN AT INTER-MILAN.

text.p: French league leaders Monaco will be looking for an away win against Internazionale in Tuesday's UEFA Cup semi-final first leg, says club coach Jean Tigana.
"So far in the Cup, we've won all our away games and we'll be trying to do the same at the San Siro.
"Whatever happens, we'll start off with the intention of imposing our game on them, of scoring and, if possible, winning", Tigana said.

Monaco are in a bouyant mood following their 2-0 win over Lille on Friday which saw them stretch their lead at the top of the table to 12 points, keeping them well on course for their first title since 1988.
Tigana's confidence is shared by Monaco's French international defender Patrick Blondeau who says: "I'm not impressed by Inter.
"We go there confident we're going to win. We know that this tie will be decided in the first leg which is good because we're better away than at home".
Monaco will be without their suspended captain Franck Dumas -- due to be replaced by the inexperienced Bruno Irles -- a player who signed his first professional contract only last month.
In attack, Monaco will probably rely on the impressive pairing of Nigerian Victor Ikpeba and Brazilian "Sonny" Anderson.
In contrast to Monaco, Inter were unimpressive when they drew 0-0 at Fiorentina on Saturday.
Inter have an almost full-strength squad but lack confidence, says their experienced French defender Jocelyn Angloma.
"Our problem will not be to get back to our best, physically, but to recover in our heads after the Fiorentina game."
Inter, currently third in the league and 10 points behind leaders Juventus, have no realistic title hopes, making Tuesday's match all the more important for them.
Inter's English coach Roy Hodgson has to choose between Marco Branco and Chilean Ivan Zamorano as partner for Maurizio Ganz in attack.
Branco, currently recovering from influenza, may be left out in favour of the Chilean while the attack will as usual be backed up by French schemer and ex-Monaco player Youri Djorkaeff.
Monaco's experienced Belgian and ex-Inter midfielder Enzo Scifo is doubtful but believes that Djorkaeff could hold the key to the game.
"Youri left for Italy at the right moment. He has improved a lot and now has become a player who can change the whole outcome of a match".
Englishman Paul Ince, Swiss Ciriaco Sforza and Argentine Javier Zanetti are likely to compliment Djorkaeff in a multinational midfield.
Probable lineups:
Internazionale: Gianluca Pagliuca; Jocelyn Angloma, Massimo Paganin, Salvatore Fresi, Alessandro Pistone; Javier Zanetti, Paul Ince, Ciriaco Sforza; Youri Djorkaeff; Maurizio Ganz, Ivan Zamorano.
Monaco: Fabien Barthez; Patrick Blondeau, Bruno Irles, Gilles Grimandi, Martin Djetou; Ali Benarbia, Emmanuel Petit, John Collins, Sylvain Legwinski; Sonny Anderson, Victor Ikpeba
